newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds rise after U.S. jobless relief.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds rise after U.S. jobless relief.

text.p: Argentine bonds rose in busy trade Friday after U.S. Treasuries firmed following the release of U.S. jobs figures.
"In principal the market is firm and it will probably continue," said the head trader at a large Argentine bank.

Anticipation before the U.S. jobs figures kept the market in narrow ranges during the last couple of sessions but with the figures out of the way the market is likely to be able to continue its recent upward trend, said traders.
The 5.5 percent dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 2 due 2001 rose $0.45 to 116.30. Argentina's FRB due 2005 rose 1/2 to 79-1/4.
Another trader said the FRB was establishing a new support level at 79 which was likely to help the local market. "The market can probably rise more during the session," said the trader.
"Global liquidity is high with local and overseas funds looking to emerging markets like Argentina," said the first trader.

Still, the announcement by Argentina's main trade union federation Thursday that it will hold another general strike later this month reminded players that there are still political risks to the government's economic policies.

President Carlos Menem delivered an impassioned speech to his Peronist Party Thursday but it is still not clear what impact it had on the members of his party who are still reluctant about the government's economic measures.
